sources.name: FCC Online Public Inspection File (OPIF) API
sources.what: every political-file document each station uploads: folder listing, change feed, and the PDFs

sources.name: FCC TV Query
sources.what: licensed full-power and Class A stations: call sign, community, transmitter, licensee, application IDs

sources.name: FCC TV service contour data
sources.what: predicted F(50,90) service contours, 360 points per station, updated daily

sources.name: NewsON
sources.what: free live and on-demand local newscast streams; station IDs collected from its public search

sources.name: FEC bulk candidate and committee master files
sources.what: federal candidates and committees for the cycle, used to resolve buyer identity

sources.name: Census county population estimates (2024 vintage)
sources.what: county population, spread into H3 cells by area share

sources.name: Census Gazetteer ZCTA and place files
sources.what: ZIP and city search without an external geocoder

sources.name: H3
sources.what: hexagonal cells used for density layers

sources.name: Nominatim (OpenStreetMap)
sources.what: fallback geocoder for street addresses only

modules.crawl:
Crawl FCC political files for stations into SQLite, optionally downloading PDFs.

  python3 -m ingest.crawl --stations 33710,66221 --years 2026 --download --workers 4

Resumable: files already listed are skipped on re-list only if --relist is absent;
downloads already on disk are never repeated.
modules.update:
Incremental updater: apply the FCC file-history change feed to the local store.

The feed (`/api/manager/file/history.json`) lists every file added, deleted,
moved, renamed or purged across all stations for a date range, with the folder
path, size and timestamps. One call per 500 rows; a peak day is ~30 pages.

  python3 -m ingest.update                       # from last sync (or yesterday) to today
  python3 -m ingest.update --since 2026-10-20    # explicit window
  python3 -m ingest.update --download --parse --aggregate   # and run the rest of the pipeline

Only tracked stations (those already in `files`) are applied unless --stations
adds more. Re-running a window is idempotent.
modules.ocr:
OCR image-only PDFs (Nexstar, Sinclair and some others file scans/prints with no text layer).

Renders pages with pypdfium2 and runs the tesseract CLI; text is cached at
data/ocr/<file_manager_id>.txt and picked up by ingest.parse.

  python3 -m ingest.ocr --workers 6          # all downloaded docs that parsed as kind=other without text
modules.parse:
Parse downloaded political-file PDFs into structured rows.

Handles the three document kinds that make up nearly all of a station's
political file when the station runs WideOrbit traffic (most do):
  * order / contract  ("CONTRACT", "Contract / Revision")
  * invoice           ("INVOICE", "Invoice #", per-spot lines with Ad-ID)
  * NAB PB-19 forms   (fillable AcroForm fields: candidate, committee, agency...)
Anything else is stored as kind=other so the gap is visible.

  python3 -m ingest.parse            # parse everything downloaded and unparsed
  python3 -m ingest.parse --file x.pdf   # print the parse of one file
modules.entities:
Rebuild domain entities from `document.raw` + `opif_file.folder_path`.

Deterministic and total: it truncates the entity tables and rebuilds them, so a parser
improvement or an alias change only needs `load_pg` + `entities`, never a recrawl.
Manual buyer merges live in data/buyer_overrides.yaml (alias -> canonical name) and are
applied on top of the automatic folder-based identity.
  python3 -m ingest.entities
modules.identity:
Buyer identity: merge the stations' own folder labels into canonical buyers and match them
to FEC candidates and committees.

Inputs: buyer_alias rows of source 'folder' (one per station label) with the station's state,
FEC bulk master files in data/fec (cn.txt candidates, cm.txt committees, ccl.txt linkage),
and data/buyer_overrides.yaml (manual: `raw label: Canonical Name`, or `category|raw label: ...`).
Output: data/buyer_identity.json, read by ingest.entities on its next run.

  python3 -m ingest.identity          # then: python3 -m ingest.entities
modules.geo:
Geography: counties with population, H3 cells with population, and station coverage shares.

  python3 -m ingest.geo            # everything (downloads Census files to data/geo on first run)

Resolutions come from HEX_RES. Coarse resolutions are built nationwide; fine ones only inside
the contours of stations that have political files loaded ("active"), so the fine layers grow
with the crawl. Adding a resolution is a one-line change here plus a rerun.
modules.aggregate:
Roll parsed documents up to spend per station per buyer and export JSON for the web app.

Spend rule, per order number within a station-year:
  * if invoices exist, spend = sum of gross over distinct invoice numbers (what actually aired)
  * else spend = gross on the latest order revision (latest print date, then latest upload)
Buyer = the leaf folder the station filed the documents under (candidate, committee or
issue sponsor), which is how station staff label buys. Category = the second folder level
(Federal / State / Local / Non-Candidate Issue Ads).

  python3 -m ingest.aggregate            # writes web/data/spend/<facility>.json and index.json
modules.export:
Export serving artifacts from the marts.

web/data/spend/<facility>.json, index.json   per-station buyers (what the map reads today)
web/data/hex/total_r<res>.json                money/ads reaching each cell (for the hex layers)
data/marts/*.parquet                          every mart, for DuckDB / the next UI / analysis
web/data/build.json                           build id + timestamp (cache busting)

python3 -m ingest.export
modules.tiles:
Vector tiles (PMTiles) for the map: hex money layers and station contours, via tippecanoe.

python3 -m ingest.tiles        -> web/data/tiles/hex5.pmtiles, hex7.pmtiles, contours.pmtiles, meta.json
modules.places:
Static place index for search: ZIP centroids and populated places from the Census Gazetteer files.
Writes web/data/places.json so the app can resolve "50309", "Des Moines" or "Des Moines, IA" with no
external geocoder. Street addresses still fall back to Nominatim in the app.

  python3 -m ingest.places
